post.caption: A Korean crown tomb honors Sweden. In 1926, Sweden's crown prince visited Korea on a world tour. Gustaf Adolf loved archaeology and joined a dig at a Silla tomb. The dig brought up a gold crown in Gyeongju. Three small gold birds perch on its tree shaped uprights. The birds were read as phoenixes, and bong is Korean for phoenix. The tomb became Seobongchong, with seo from the Chinese word for Sweden. Chong is the Korean word for a tomb. The prince later became King Gustaf VI Adolf. In 1994, his grandson, King Carl XVI Gustaf, visited the tomb site.
